title: Bind qa_approve to the exact candidate the reviewer read
description:
Objective: make an approval apply to the bytes the reviewer actually read. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaApprove.ts today checks status and a summary, so an approval issued against one candidate silently blesses whatever the task holds by the time it lands.

Deliverable: qa_approve accepts the reviewed candidate id and rejects the call when that candidate is not the task's current one, with a named error telling the reviewer to re-read. get_context surfaces the current candidate id to QA so the reviewer has it. A Review record is persisted carrying reviewer, decision, the exact reviewed candidate and the summary, and qa_reject records the same binding.

Not in scope: the delivery-evidence gate on DONE, which is the sibling task, and any IDE change. Keep qa_approve's existing soft commit-evidence warnings working; this task adds a hard binding on candidate identity only.

Unskips the acceptance case "reviewing candidate A cannot approve B".

Verification: npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: qa_approve accepts a reviewed candidate id and rejects a mismatch against the task's current candidate with a named error, asserted exactly
qa_reject records the same candidate binding as qa_approve
A Review record persisting reviewer, decision, reviewed candidate and summary is written for both outcomes
get_context returns the current candidate id for a task in REVIEW
A project with no candidate recorded keeps the current approve behaviour, so adoption is incremental
The acceptance case for reviewing candidate A cannot approve B is unskipped and passes unchanged
npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: Keep the existing qa_approve warnings array and commitEvidence; this task adds a hard candidate binding, it does not restructure the tool's result.
A task with no candidate recorded must keep working, so the change is additive.

implementationPlan.description: READ THE FROZEN CONTRACT BEFORE WRITING A LINE. Read-only, no edits. This task's shape is dictated, not chosen: packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts was authored before any implementation so no later task could redefine delivery, and its rules say a diff that edits an assertion, constant, fixture or helper in that file instead of the code under test is a QA reject. You may change exactly one character in it - the skip on your own case. (a) Read its header, lines 1-70, and transcribe the four normative items that belong to this task into the step note verbatim: moe.qa_approve also accepts candidateId; moe.get_context projects result.currentCandidate as the exact stored Candidate record selected by createdAt then id; the persisted Review carries taskId, candidateId, reviewerId, decision and summary; CANDIDATE_MISMATCH maps to MoeErrorCode -32002. Note also that every new record lives at .moe/<kind>/<id>.json following the resourceStore pattern, so reviews go in .moe/reviews. (b) Read criterion 3 in full, lines 1435-1625, and write down what it asserts BEYOND this card's Definition of Done, because those assertions are binding too: the refusal's context must carry expectedCandidateId and currentCandidateId with exactly those key names; currentCandidate must deep-equal the whole stored candidate file, not just an id; on refusal the task file bytes, BOTH candidate files and an EMPTY reviews directory must all hold; and the positive control expects exactly one review record after approving the current candidate. (c) Read src/tools/qaApprove.ts (179 lines) whole - its result literal at line 155 carries warnings, commitEvidence and message, and a task rail forbids restructuring it. Read src/tools/qaReject.ts and the tail of src/tools/getContext.ts, whose single large return literal begins at line 271. (d) Read src/state/candidateStore.ts and note its exact export list - a test in the candidate task pins it at five exports, so do not add a sixth; listCandidatesForTask already orders by createdAt then id, which is exactly the selection rule, so REUSE it rather than sorting again. (e) Note what NOT to do: ATTEMPT_FINALIZING lives in src/util/claimGuards.ts and gates claiming, not approving, and criterion 3 deliberately finalizes the attempt so that hold is not the refusing layer. Do not fence qa_approve on attempt identity - QA is not the attempt holder, and assertAttemptCurrent here would break the case.

PERSIST THE REVIEW RECORD. In src/types/schema.ts add an exported Review interface carrying id, taskId, candidateId, reviewerId, decision and createdAt, plus the summary, with decision a union of approve and reject. The five field names the acceptance case projects are fixed by the frozen contract; id and createdAt are the record's own, matching every other store. Keep it additive: no existing type changes, no schemaVersion bump, no migration. In src/state/StateManager.ts add a reviews map beside the existing candidates map and one loadEntities call over the reviews directory in load, exactly as the candidates collection was wired. Create src/state/reviewStore.ts as stateless exported functions taking the state handle first, mirroring candidateStore: record, get and a list by task. Reviews are an append-only audit trail, so there is NO update and NO delete function - the function must not exist, which is stronger than a convention not to call one, and a reopened task that is reviewed again simply gets a second record. Persist with writeEntity BEFORE touching the map, so a failed write leaves no review visible. Error handling: validate that taskId, candidateId, reviewerId and summary are non-blank strings and that the decision is one of the two members, refusing with the invalid-input error rather than coercing. Do NOT add a separate reviewStore test file - the named verification command covers src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts and the acceptance file, so the store's cases live in the former.

PROJECT THE CURRENT CANDIDATE FROM get_context. In src/tools/getContext.ts add currentCandidate as a top-level key on the result literal that begins at line 271. Its value is the task's current candidate record - the last one by createdAt then id - obtained through candidateStore's existing list-by-task function so the ordering rule lives in one place and cannot drift from the record_candidate side. Emit the WHOLE stored record, not a projection and not just an id: the acceptance case deep-equals it against the candidate file on disk, so any reshaping or added field fails it. Omit the key entirely when the task has no candidate, rather than emitting null, so a project that has never recorded one sees no change at all. Include it whenever a candidate exists regardless of status, which necessarily covers the REVIEW case the Definition of Done names and also helps a worker about to record a second candidate; a status gate would make the field vanish exactly when a reviewer re-reads a reopened task. Hand out a copy rather than the live cached object, the way the candidate task's own review insisted, so a caller cannot mutate stored state through the response. Change nothing else in that literal - it is the payload every role reads at the start of every task.

BIND BOTH QA DECISIONS TO THE REVIEWED CANDIDATE. In src/tools/qaApprove.ts accept an optional candidateId argument and resolve the task's current candidate through the same list-by-task helper. Decide in this order. If the task has NO candidate at all, behave exactly as today, which is the additive-adoption rail - a project that never records candidates must keep working. If a candidateId is supplied and it does not match the current candidate's id, refuse BEFORE any write with a MoeError carrying the existing state-conflict numeric code, the stable codeName CANDIDATE_MISMATCH, and a context holding exactly expectedCandidateId - what the reviewer read - and currentCandidateId; the message should tell the reviewer to re-read the current candidate, because that is the action. If it matches, proceed. If a candidate exists but candidateId was OMITTED, proceed - adoption is incremental - but push a warning onto the existing warnings array so the gap is visible rather than silent; that array already exists for the commit-evidence warning and a rail forbids restructuring the result, so add to it and change nothing else about warnings, commitEvidence or message. On every successful approval write one Review with decision approve, and write it only after the candidate check has passed, since the acceptance case asserts an EMPTY reviews directory after a refusal. Apply the identical argument, the identical refusal and an identical Review with decision reject in src/tools/qaReject.ts, leaving its existing reopen and failed-item behaviour untouched. Do not add an attempt fence to either tool.

TEST IT, THEN UNSKIP THE ACCEPTANCE CASE AND OWE THE RED. Extend src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts with the unit-level matrix, asserting exact values and, for every refusal, BOTH the numeric code and the exact codeName string, since several codes share a number here. Cover: a matching candidate approves and writes exactly one review with the five contract fields; a mismatched candidate refuses with CANDIDATE_MISMATCH carrying both context keys, and afterwards the task bytes on disk and the reviews directory are untouched; a task with no candidate approves exactly as before, with the result's warnings, commitEvidence and message shape unchanged, which is the adoption rail; a candidate that exists with the id omitted approves but adds the warning; a supplied id naming a candidate that belongs to a DIFFERENT task is a mismatch, not a match; malformed input is refused rather than coerced; qa_reject records a review with decision reject and refuses the same mismatch; and an injected writeEntity failure on the review leaves no review visible and is surfaced rather than swallowed. Then change the single skip on criterion 3 in src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts and NOTHING else in that file - no assertion, constant, fixture or helper. Owe the red properly: before the production change is complete, run that case unskipped and record it failing at the counterexample the describe names, which is the wrong-candidate approval reaching DONE on bytes nobody reviewed. Take that red in a throwaway copy or a scratch worktree, never by editing the shared checkout's assertions. Run the named command, npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts, and require green with the criterion-3 case now executing rather than skipped - check the skipped count actually dropped by one.

DOCUMENT, GATE, REVIEW, HAND OFF. (a) Add a Review section to docs/SCHEMA.md beside the Candidate section the sibling task added, covering every field, the append-only rule with the explicit statement that a re-review appends rather than edits, and the storage location. In docs/MCP_SERVER.md extend the qa_approve and qa_reject sections with the candidateId argument, the CANDIDATE_MISMATCH refusal and its two context keys, the incremental-adoption behaviour when a project records no candidates, and the new currentCandidate projection on get_context. Both documents are contended by sibling Wave 1 cards, so re-read the landed text immediately before editing and add rather than restructure. (b) Run the named verification, then the full daemon suite from the repository root with npm.cmd on Windows, requiring exit 0 and a total no lower than before minus nothing - the skipped count should drop by one and the passed count rise. Filter for the summary lines but capture the exit code in a separate statement, because a filtered pipeline swallows it. Note that the suite has been observed flaking under heavy fleet load; if a file unrelated to this change fails, re-run that file alone before treating it as yours. Run npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json and require exit 0. (c) Adversarially review: can an approval ever reach DONE on a candidate the reviewer did not name; is the refusal genuinely before every write, proven by the untouched bytes and the empty reviews directory rather than only by the thrown error; does a project with no candidates behave byte-identically to before; is currentCandidate the whole record, a copy rather than the live object, and absent rather than null when there is none; is the selection rule shared with record_candidate rather than duplicated; does the review store truly lack an update path; did the qa_approve result keep its warnings, commitEvidence and message shape; and was the acceptance file changed by exactly one skip. (d) Note the file count honestly in the completion summary: ten files, which trips the size warning, because the Definition of Done requires the record, its store, both decision tools, the context projection, the unit matrix, the acceptance unskip and both contract documents. Complete through moe.complete_task with the commands, exit codes, counts and the recorded red, listing every modified path.

Keep the gate itself as it is: its order, the Review-before-updateTask write, currentCandidate in get_context and the acceptance unskip all hold. The fix is tests plus doc lines, plus one decision on the extra warning branch.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Refusing when a candidate exists but candidateId was omitted - rejected by the additive-adoption rail and by the Definition of Done, which requires existing behaviour to survive; instead the omission proceeds and pushes a line onto the warnings array the tool already has, so the gap is visible without becoming a hard gate. That mirrors how the plan-revision work treated an absent token as legacy. Recomputing the current candidate with a fresh sort inside qa_approve - rejected: two definitions of current will diverge, so the existing list-by-task helper is the single source. Projecting only the candidate id from get_context - rejected outright: the acceptance case deep-equals the whole record against the file, and the card's Definition of Done wording is the looser of the two. Gating the projection on REVIEW status - rejected: always emitting it when a candidate exists satisfies the Definition of Done, helps a worker recording a second candidate, and avoids the field vanishing when a reopened task is re-read. Giving the review store an update path for a re-review - rejected: reviews are an append-only audit trail, so a second review is a second record and the update function must not exist at all. Adding a separate reviewStore test file - rejected: it would push the file count past the hard limit, and the named verification command only reads qaApprove.test.ts and the acceptance file.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Both dependencies landed and QA-approved, so this task builds on known bytes rather than declared intent. The Candidate record is frozen at seven fields and its store exports exactly five functions, pinned by a test, so nothing here may extend it. Its list-by-task function already sorts by createdAt then id, which is precisely the current-candidate selection rule the frozen contract names - reusing it keeps one definition of current instead of two that can drift. The acceptance file is the real specification and it is stricter than this card's Definition of Done in two places worth calling out: get_context must project the WHOLE stored candidate record, deep-equal to the file on disk, not merely an id as the Definition of Done says, and the refusal's error context must carry exactly expectedCandidateId and currentCandidateId. It also asserts the reviews directory is EMPTY after a refusal, which forces the candidate check ahead of every write rather than merely ahead of the status change. One trap: the finalizing hold introduced by the sibling finalize task lives in claimGuards and gates claiming, and criterion 3 deliberately finalizes the attempt so that hold is not what refuses - adding an attempt fence to qa_approve would break the case and is conceptually wrong anyway, since QA never holds the attempt.
planningNotes.risks: Ten distinct files trips the size warning and sits one under the hard rejection limit, which is why there is no separate store test file and no extra helper - the Definition of Done genuinely requires the record, its store, both decision tools, the context projection, the unit matrix, the acceptance unskip and both contract documents. The single largest hazard is editing the acceptance file beyond its skip: its own rules make that an automatic QA reject, so the worker must treat every assertion, constant and fixture there as read-only. The second is ordering: the candidate check must precede every write, and the proof is the untouched task bytes plus an empty reviews directory, not merely a thrown error. Do not add an attempt fence to qa_approve. Keep the result literal's warnings, commitEvidence and message untouched. Hand out a copy of the candidate record rather than the cached object. Both documents are contended by sibling Wave 1 cards, so re-read before editing. Finally, the full suite has been observed flaking under heavy fleet load, so re-run a failing unrelated file alone before attributing it to this change.
